rationale: Round 3 re-review of the branch-vs-base diff after the two prior rounds' CR-001 (isMeta/isSidechain skip, then message-less system-line skip) were fixed on commits c312d858 and 4a64d708. All three lenses ran with parseable output against the scoped production diff (docs/ARCHITECTURE-OTLP-PLUGIN.md, session-signals.ts + tests, claude-named-invocations.ts + tests; the remainder of the branch-vs-base diff is this branch's own sdlc-light run bookkeeping artifacts, excluded from lens review as non-functional). Acceptance ran against both Jira tickets' criteria: all of EPMCDME-15582's ACs pass, and the acceptance lens marked the 15-Nov regression scenario 'partial' only because the included tests don't reproduce the exact 7-vs-5 combination from the Jira comment — not required by this diff's own stated review focus, and the underlying mechanism (LOCAL_ONLY_COMMANDS denylist) is directly tested for every individual command named in that regression, so this is not blocking. EPMCDME-17201's client-observable ACs (3, 4, 5) pass; ACs 1/2 and the backend/UI regression-test requests are correctly 'na' (backend cli_analytics_handler.py / Session Detail UI, a different repo, per the ticket's own description). Nine lens concerns were triaged to dismiss, none blocking: (1) the `../../claude/session/...` relative import — an existing precedent in the same directory (fork-skill.ts already imports the same symbol the same way) and already documented in ARCHITECTURE-OTLP-PLUGIN.md, an accepted design choice from the prior round; (2) wrappedCommandName/matchCommandNames returning only the first match per line and recordCommand reusing one fromIndex for multiple commands in one message — both already triaged dismiss in the prior round as matching the codebase's one-command-per-turn invariant and being very low real-world frequency; (3) the text-wide (not tag-paired) genuine-wrapper check in wrappedCommandName — mirrors the pre-existing matchCommandNames pattern it was extracted from, not a new risk; (4) no cross-repo sync mechanism for LOCAL_ONLY_COMMANDS vs the backend SENTINEL_EXACT list — an explicit, already-documented, user-approved tradeoff carried over unchanged since round 1; (5) nextSkillName's unbounded forward scan (worst-case O(n) per command) — realistic sessions have at most tens of slash commands, no real performance risk, already dismissed in round 2; (6) case-sensitivity mismatch between a command name and its dispatched skill name, and between wrappedCommandName's output and LOCAL_ONLY_COMMANDS's lowercase entries — command/skill names are CLI-literal and always lower-case, already dismissed in round 2; (7) a hypothetical empty-content-array ([]) user message defeating isToolResultOnlyMessage — purely speculative, no evidence any real transcript produces this shape; (8) isSidechain only consulted inside nextSkillName's lookahead, not in the main extraction loop's isUser branch — pre-existing behavior unchanged by this diff (the original scanCommands was equally sidechain-unaware), not a regression introduced here; (9) the edge-case lens's most substantive concern — that nextSkillName does not skip a non-meta, non-sidechain 'self-written' user line (e.g. `<local-command-stdout>`, `<bash-stdout>`) the way countTurns's SELF_WRITTEN_PREFIXES does — was verified directly against this repo's own fixture (tests/integration/session/fixtures/session-3fe1b6bc.jsonl, lines 3-4): such lines are real (isMeta is unset, confirmed via a repo-wide scan finding no fixture occurrence with isMeta:true) but only ever follow a LOCAL_ONLY-style purely-local command (`/clear`'s own echoed stdout in that fixture) which never dispatches a Skill and so never needs the dedup to fire; the fixture's only skill/workflow-dispatching command (line 6, a bmad workflow slash command) is followed by the isMeta:true caveat wrapper already handled by the existing skip, not a bare self-written line. Since a skill-backed command never produces a self-written local-command echo of its own (that pattern is specific to commands that execute entirely client-side), this gap cannot actually reach the EPMCDME-17201 failure mode it would need to reach to matter — dismissed as unreachable rather than merely low-frequency. No decision_needed findings remain. All three standards checks (commit format, code quality, security) pass: all 8 commits on this branch follow Conventional Commits with correct ticket references; no `any`/unsafe types introduced; no secrets, injection, or unsafe I/O in the pure in-memory diff.
